collector_findings: One SingleThreadedExecutor processes subscriptions. The while loop calls spin_once with at most0.1s timeout; this timeout is a wait bound, not an unconditional100ms sleep or10Hz throttle.

Each callback stores monotonic receipt time and header stamp; joints copy arrays and IMU converts the message to a dictionary. No explicit per-message sleep exists. Finite processing time can still matter.
The subscription uses qos_profile_sensor_data. Its effective QoS and publisher endpoints were not recorded; loss/backlog cannot be excluded.

The final report discards full receipt/header arrays and retains count, first/last stamps, maximum receipt gap, monotonicity count, and only the last payload. Thus no interval histogram, correlation of missing intervals, jitter, per-message delivery lag, or repeated-sample timing can be reconstructed.
Header span is slightly longer than callback span; bounded discovery/startup backlog can compress receipt density. This does not explain or diagnose the residual rate shortfall.
conclusion: The approximately249Hz receipt counts do not establish a520Hz controller-loop failure. Both broadcasters were explicitly configured260Hz. The sensor reports are separately requested100Hz. A short lossy observer summary cannot distinguish controller scheduling/decimation, realtime publication skips, DDS loss, or callback backlog.
driver_and_publication_findings: Each normal driver read invokes one spi_driver_run, which performs two board ioctl transfers, then copies actuator states. write copies commands for a subsequent read transfer. There is no normal-path fixed sleep that directly sets250Hz in the inspected driver.

IMU read returns the mutex-protected cached sampler result; it computes measurement age from a host packet receipt timestamp minus device-provided age. The age is exported as imu_sensor/time_since_measurement_seconds; raw packet/measurement timestamp state exports are commented out.

The IMU message does not include this age state or independent sensor sequence identity. Equal quaternion/gyro values alone cannot prove stale sampling, because a stationary quantized sensor may legitimately repeat them.
Accelerometer reporting is deliberately not enabled in the inspected transport; the zero acceleration payload is not a new observed publication-rate fault.

The actual console records failure to obtain FIFO scheduling. This is a real configuration observation, but causation of the249Hz receipts is unproven and no permission/RT changes are justified by this analysis.
explicit_nonclaims: No verified fresh IMU sampling rate.
No conclusion that FIFO denial caused the message-rate shortfall.
No multiplier-based estimate of actual manager rate from249Hz receipts.
No hardware or policy readiness approval.

minimum_next_passive_capture.action: Read exact update_rate/is_async/use_sim_time parameters for manager and broadcasters, actual publisher/subscriber QoS/endpoints, and installed package versions. No parameter writes.

If manager periodicity/execution diagnostics or statistics are already published by the installed version, record them in the same interval. Their direct cycle-rate evidence is more informative than multiplying topic counts. Do not add a new controller, enable instrumentation, or change configuration for this capture.

If an existing dynamic-state publisher already exposes imu_sensor/time_since_measurement_seconds, record its full values/timestamps. Otherwise mark IMU age unavailable; do not pretend the Imu header supplies sample identity. Adding an age publisher would be a separate reviewed instrumentation change.

Compare receipt and header delta distributions, cross-topic synchronized gaps, and direct manager statistics if available. Preserve the manager console for overruns. If only topic timestamps exist, report publication/delivery behavior and keep exact control-loop rate unresolved.
